items.title: Beam Time Manager User Guide
items.text:
Beam Time Manager (BTM) accounts for how Jefferson Lab's accelerator and experimental halls spend their time, hour by hour. At the end of each shift the Crew Chief and each hall fill out a timesheet, started from automated measurements; BTM cross-checks the two against each other and against Downtime Manager (DTM); and the reports turn the saved timesheets into the beam time, availability and schedule figures that lab management reviews. BTM also keeps the accelerator's program as a State Timeline, and the NPES schedule.

At JLab, BTM is at ace.jlab.org/btm. You can view it without logging in; log in to make changes.

The guide's website has a copy for each release; pick the version the Help tab shows. On GitHub, this guide describes the main branch, which may be newer than the version you are using.

items.title: Contents
items.text:
1. Concepts: modes, programs and states, the schedules, planned, measured and reported values, the derived metrics, and roles.
  2. Timesheets: filling out, saving and signing the Crew Chief and experimenter timesheets. For Crew Chiefs and the halls.
  3. Cross-checks: how the Crew Chief's figures are compared with the halls' and with DTM, and resolving discrepancies.
  4. State Timeline: the accelerator program over time, and correcting it.
  5. Schedule and programs: the NPES schedule's versions, editing and publishing it, and the hall programs. For the scheduling committee.
  6. Reports: the Reports tab, and how it counts.
  7. Administration: roles, the Setup tab and settings. For administrators.
  8. Common issues: situations that come up again and again, and how to record them.

items.title: Tabs at a glance
items.text: Tab What it is for State Timeline The accelerator program now and in the past; Crew Chiefs correct it here. Timesheets The Crew Chief and experimenter timesheets, shift by shift. Schedule The NPES schedule, month by month. Programs Each hall's programs: experiments and other tasks. Metrics A glossary of the hall, multiplicity and experimenter states. Reports Beam time, physics, availability and charge reports, the review calendar, the activity audit and the EPICS connection status. Setup Administrators only: settings, runs and the user directory cache. Help Version, contacts, documentation and a feedback form.

items.title: Quick start for Crew Chiefs
items.text:
1. During the shift, check that the State Timeline shows the right program, and correct it if not.
  2. Before the end of the shift, ask each hall to save all but the last hour of its timesheet.
  3. At the end of the shift, open Timesheets: during the first hour of the next shift it opens the one that just ended.
  4. On the Hourly tab, check the Reported hours of the accelerator, each hall and the multiplicity; edit the wrong ones, and save. Fill out the Shift Information.
  5. Check the cross-checks. Resolve discrepancies with the halls, or explain them in Crew Chief Comments.
  6. Sign. BTM saves whatever is still unsaved and posts a summary to the logbook.

items.title: Quick start for the halls
items.text:
1. Open Timesheets, choose your hall's experimenter timesheet, or bookmark it from Current Shift (bookmarkable).
  2. Before the end of the shift, use Edit CC Hours to check and save all but the last hour, for the Crew Chief.
  3. After the shift ends, check and save every hour: ABU, BANU, BNA and OFF, and ER, PCC, UED and OFF, each adding up to one hour.
  4. Explain any UED with Reasons not Ready, fill out the Shift Information, and Sign.

See Timesheets for the details.

items.title: Questions and changes
items.text:
Use the feedback form on the Help tab, or contact the content and technical contacts listed there. To suggest a change to this guide, open an issue or pull request on GitHub.

This guide replaces the "Machine Time Accounting User Guide" (version 13, August 2025); its definitions and common issues are included here.

items.title: Administration
items.text:
User Guide › Administration

For BTM's administrators, the Operability managers.

items.title: Roles
items.text:
BTM's roles are kept in JLab's single sign-on (Keycloak). A change to someone's roles takes effect when they next log in.

Role Name in BTM Can btm-admin Operability Manager Everything below, and the Setup tab. Signs timesheets as Operability Manager, and writes Reviewer Comments on cross-checks. cc Crew Chief Edit and sign Crew Chief timesheets; correct the State Timeline; edit the programs; reset the EPICS connection on CA Status. schcom Committee Member Create, upload, edit and publish schedules, including tentative ones; edit the programs. halead, hblead, hclead, hdlead Hall A, B, C, D Manager Change their hall's experimenter timesheets after they are locked to their signer, 48 hours after the shift started. (any logged-in user) User Edit and sign experimenter timesheets; see the Activity Audit; send feedback.

Everyone can view the timesheets, State Timeline, published schedules, programs, metrics and reports without logging in.

An administrator's signature locks an experimenter timesheet: then only administrators can change it.

items.title: Setup
items.text: The Setup tab, for administrators only, has three pages.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The settings are kept in the database. Filter by key or tag, and edit a value. A change made on the page takes effect at once; one made directly in the database takes effect after Refresh Cache or a redeploy.

Key Meaning ADMIN_ROLE_NAME The administrators' role, btm-admin. The Help tab lists its members, and feedback goes to them. HELP_CONTENT_CONTACT, HELP_TECHNICAL_CONTACT The contacts the Help tab shows. HELP_DOC_CSV The Help tab's documentation links: a comma-separated list of URL\|Label. HALL_AVAIL_DOC_URL The Hall Availability report's Explanation link. MYQUERY_SERVER_URL The EPICS archiver web service the Charge report reads. NOTIFICATION_ENABLED, NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE, NOTIFICATION_LINK_NAME, NOTIFICATION_LINK_URL A banner across every page, such as for planned maintenance. EMAIL_ENABLED, EMAIL_TESTING_ENABLED, EMAIL_DOMAIN_NAME, EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS Email, such as the feedback form. In testing mode, all mail goes to the testers. IP_READ_FILTER_ENABLED, IP_READ_ALLOWLIST_PATTERN, IP_READ_URL_PATTERN Let computers at allowed addresses view pages that need a login. Takes effect after a redeploy. SMOOTHNESS_CDN_ENABLED, SMOOTHNESS_SERVER Where the pages' shared styles and scripts are loaded from.

items.title: Runs
items.text:
A run is a stretch of days the accelerator is scheduled to be on: consecutive days whose program is not OFF in each month's latest published schedule. A day, or a month, with no published schedule counts as OFF. The reports' date pickers offer the current and previous runs as Current Run and Previous Run, and the Charge report opens on the current run.

BTM works the runs out again whenever a schedule is published and when the app starts; Recalculate from Schedules does it now. The page shows the Current Run and Previous Run, and lists every run:

Column Meaning First Day, Last Day, Days The run's days. Source Schedule, worked out from the published schedules, or Set by hand. Published Schedules What the published schedules have for the run: Same, other days, or No run.

When the actual run differs from the schedule, such as a restore that started two days before the NPES schedule had it, select the run and Edit its First Day and Last Day, or Add a run. A run set by hand stays as it is when the schedules change, and takes the place of any scheduled run that shares its days; two runs can't share a day. Remove a run set by hand to go back to the schedule. A run from the schedules can't be removed, since recalculating would add it again: edit it instead.

items.title: Directory Cache
items.text: BTM caches users and roles from single sign-on; the cache is cleared every night. Users and Roles show what is cached. Search for a user or role to add them to the cache, or Clear it, such as after a change to someone's roles.

items.title: Server settings
items.text:
Some settings are the server's, set where BTM is deployed, not on the Setup tab:

Setting Meaning BTM_EPICS_ADDR_LIST Where BTM finds the EPICS PVs it measures from. BTM_PROGRAM_PV The PV the State Timeline is recorded from. If it is not set, the timeline is kept by hand. LOGBOOK_SERVER_URL, LOGBOOK_DEBUG The logbook server signed timesheets post to; with LOGBOOK_DEBUG on, entries go to the TLOG test logbook. JLAB_RUN_URL Where the date pickers find the current and previous runs.

The PD shift plans and DTM's events are read from their own databases.

See the README for all of them.

items.title: Reasons not ready
items.text: The reasons that experimenters choose to explain UED (Unplanned Experiment Down), on the experimenter timesheet, are kept per hall in the database; there is no page for them. Inactive reasons are not offered.

items.title: Help tab
items.text: The Help tab shows BTM's version and release date, the content and technical contacts, the administrators (when logged in), the documentation links from HELP_DOC_CSV, and a feedback form that emails the administrators.

items.title: Common issues
items.text:
User Guide › Common issues

Situations that come up again and again in time accounting, and how to record them.

items.title: Bonus ABU
items.text: A hall sometimes records more ABU than the Crew Chief's Up and Tune, or records ABU during beam studies. It looks like a gift, but it complicates the numbers. The cross-checks are lenient about it; make sure it really is bonus beam and not a data error.

items.title: Opportunistic beam studies during a long downtime
items.text: When a major failure causes a long downtime, the machine is often kept busy with an alternative program. That's good, but keep recording Down: hall Down (BNA) if the program is Physics, or Internal Down if it is Internal. If the program really is changed, then record the downtime in DTM as Non-Program. Otherwise BTM and DTM disagree: downtime in DTM while BTM says the machine was Off, for example, breaks the availability figures.

items.title: Whose downtime is it?
items.text: The choice between BANU and BNA depends on where the failed component is. Who maintains it, owns it or paid for it doesn't matter: a component located in the hall makes BANU, and one located in the accelerator makes BNA. As in DTM, a failure that doesn't stop the program isn't a blocking DTM event; keep recording Up and ABU. DTM can still record it as non-program downtime.

items.title: Do trips count as down?
items.text: Yes: in total they add up to a lot of time. BOOM switches to Down on a trip, even when the Crew Chief has forced a mode, and DTM records each trip's duration too. Some reports, such as DTM's Joule report, leave trips out.

items.title: Restore: BTM, DTM and after studies
items.text: BTM's NPES Restore is the initial restore at the start of a run, as scheduled by the NPES. DTM's restore is the recovery after a component failure. Restoring after beam studies is not a state of its own: it is still Studies. So if the PD's plan says beam studies until 5 and restore to physics until 6, record Studies until 6.

items.title: Hall tuning, accelerator tuning and perfection tuning
items.text:
Accelerator tuning sets up the accelerator, up to but not into a hall, to the program's requirements. Hall tuning sets up the hall's own equipment.

Crew Chief Hall Accelerator tuning Down, or Internal Down in Internal mode BNA if the hall expects beam, otherwise Off Hall tuning Up or Tune (tuning can use CW or pulsed beam) ABU

A hall that receives beam meeting the agreed program requirements may still ask for better beam. The PD then decides between quantity and quality, which is harder when the other halls are happy with the beam. The Director of Operations has the final say.

items.title: Time-restricted states
items.text: NPES Restore and ACC each have an allowance (see Restore, ACC and their allowances). It's hard to remember the allowances and to switch to Internal Down once one is used up. An auditor can look at the data afterwards for Restore or ACC time beyond the allowance.

items.title: Which plan decides?
items.text:
Many states depend on the plan: a hall records BNA when it expects beam and doesn't get it. But who decides whether the hall should expect it?

  • The plans are coarse. The NPES schedule, the whiteboard and the PD shift plan say how many hours a hall gets in a shift, not which ones. The PD, the Crew Chief and the hall may need to talk it through.
  • The plan changes quickly. If the whiteboard gives Hall A beam tomorrow, but a failure in the accelerator today means it won't get it, does Hall A record Down or Off tomorrow?

BOOM's rule is that Off must be decided at least 8 hours in advance. As with opportunistic beam studies, changing the plan can hide downtime. Generally record Down, and keep the machine busy with opportunistic studies if possible (not recorded as scheduled studies). If the program really is changed to scheduled studies, stop recording the downtime in DTM.

items.title: Møller measurements
items.text: The Crew Chief records Up or Tune; the hall records ABU. The hall may record more ABU than the Crew Chief's Up and Tune, since setting up takes time and trips may not show on the operations side while the hall records ABU for the whole interval. The Crew Chief resolves it by raising Up or Tune to match the ABU.

items.title: BNA during Internal mode
items.text: During a scheduled Internal program, such as NPES Restore or Studies, the halls are not scheduled for physics beam: they record Off, not BNA.

items.title: Trusting the automated accounting
items.text: The measured values are a starting point. If your hall received beam and used it in any way, such as for a Møller measurement, a target position scan or a current calibration, that time is ABU, and you will probably have to enter it yourself: the automated accounting usually gets procedures wrong. If your hall is scheduled to be off, the Crew Chief may force the hall's Off mode in BOOM, which in effect turns the automated accounting off.

items.title: Known difficulties
items.text:
• The cross-checks are complex. The Crew Chief and the halls don't measure the same things, so the figures can't simply be compared.
  • End-of-shift cross-checks come late, as the Crew Chief is trying to leave. Comparing hour by hour during the shift avoids that, at the cost of more calls between the Crew Chief and the halls; the timesheets support it.
  • Checking beam quality may need disruptive diagnostics.
  • Not all ABU is equal: some programs are harder to deliver than others, and the figures don't weight them.

items.title: Concepts
items.text: User Guide › Concepts

items.title: Why account for beam time
items.text:
Time accounting gathers data about how the accelerator is used and how available it is, so that lab leadership can track and monitor performance. It is kept from two perspectives:

  • Operations (Accelerator Division): the Crew Chief accounts for the accelerator's time and for the beam each hall received.
  • The halls (Physics Division): each hall's experimenters account for the beam their hall could use and did use.

Time is accounted per hour: each figure is the time within the hour that the machine, or a hall, was in a particular state. The hours are grouped into eight-hour shift timesheets. To keep the bookkeeping light, automated time accounting measures a best-effort figure for every hour, and the timekeepers correct it where it is wrong.

BTM is not Downtime Manager (DTM). DTM records each failure separately, by system and component; BTM accounts for the hours of the program. The two are linked (BTM reads DTM's downtime to measure Internal Down), but DTM's failure records are not meant to add up to BTM's hours.

items.title: Modes, states and programs
items.text:
Term Meaning Mode The machine is always in exactly one of three time accounting modes: Physics, Internal or Off. State What the machine or a hall was doing within a mode, such as Up, BNR or Internal Down. Counting the time in each state is the core of time accounting. Most states are mutually exclusive, so the states of an hour add up to one hour; Down Hard and the multiplicity states are exceptions. Program The mode, or the more specific state, that is scheduled. The accelerator has a program, and when it is Physics each hall may have its own program: an experiment, or a task such as commissioning or maintenance.

In Physics mode the machine is provided to the Physics Division, which does not by itself mean that research is being done. In Internal mode the Accelerator Division uses the machine itself: for beam studies, a configuration change (pass or energy change), or restoring the machine after it was off. In Off mode the machine is off.

On the State Timeline and the timesheets, the accelerator program is one of five, fixed (the schedule has a few more, such as FACDEV and TBD):

Program Mode Meaning Physics Physics Beam is scheduled for the halls. Studies Internal The machine is studied, tested or developed as planned (beam studies, machine development). Recovering to physics after studies is still Studies. NPES Restore Internal The machine is restored after being off, as planned. See Restore. ACC Internal Accelerator Configuration Change: the machine is being configured for a different pass or energy. Off Off The machine is off as planned, for a holiday, the budget or the schedule (not for a failure); also called Scheduled Accelerator Maintenance (SAM).

Hall programs are kept on the Programs tab and scheduled on the Schedule tab. Other JLab facilities, such as LERF, UITF, CMTF and VTA, are not part of time accounting.

items.title: Schedules
items.text:
Several schedules, each more detailed than the last, say what the machine should be doing:

  1. The NPES schedule (Nuclear Physics Experiment Scheduling committee) plans months: the accelerator program and each hall's program, day by day. BTM keeps it on the Schedule tab.
  2. The MCC whiteboard plans weeks.
  3. The Program Deputy (PD) shift plan plans days: the hours of each program in a shift. BTM shows it as the Planned values of a timesheet.
  4. The Crew Chief decides minute by minute, guided by the plans before.

The more detailed plans follow the less detailed ones, but they may differ in practice: a run may start a few days earlier than the NPES schedule said, or a hall planned for beam at 3 PM may be ready a few hours early.

The workflow, from the schedule to the reports:

  1. The Program Advisory Committee (PAC) and Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) work with the hall liaisons to review, approve and schedule experiments, and the NPES schedule is published.
  2. Operability staff make the whiteboard schedule from it.
  3. The PD makes the shift plan from the whiteboard.
  4. The Crew Chief runs the program in the shift plan, and watches the automated time accounting (BOOM) during the shift.
  5. At the end of the shift, the Crew Chief checks the timesheet, filled in from the automated accounting, and corrects it.
  6. The Crew Chief calls the halls to fill out their timesheets, compares their figures with the cross-checks and resolves differences.
  7. The Crew Chief signs the timesheet, which makes a logbook entry.
  8. The PD presents BTM's reports in the daily and weekly meetings.

items.title: Planned, measured and reported
items.text:
A timesheet has up to three values for each figure:

Value Where it comes from Planned The PD shift plan. Measured Automated time accounting: for the Crew Chief, BOOM (Beam Objective Operational Monitor) and the State Timeline; for the halls, the halls' EPICS time accounting. Reported What the timekeeper saved. This is the official figure the reports use.

Until a timekeeper saves an hour, the timesheet shows its measured values as the reported ones, to start from; the reports count only saved hours.

items.title: Automated time accounting
items.text:
BOOM is the Crew Chief's automated time accounting. It works out the operations states of each hour from diagnostics, the state of the Fast ShutDown (FSD) system, and modes the Crew Chief can force when the automatic choice is wrong (BNR, Down and Off). BOOM switches to Down on a trip, even when a mode is forced.

The halls' automated time accounting runs in EPICS IOCs. Each hall sets two PVs, beam present and beam used, and the IOCs combine them with BOOM's forced ACC, BANU and Off modes. When nothing else is measured, the hour is BNA. Two problems are common: beam used often watches only the data acquisition, so energy measurements and other procedures are left out, and beam present measures whether beam is actually there, not whether the Crew Chief could send it.

The accelerator program comes from the State Timeline, which follows the program PV and which Crew Chiefs can correct.

items.title: Accelerator states
items.text: The Crew Chief's timesheet uses these states.

items.title: Internal mode
items.text: State Meaning Studies As planned: the machine is studied, tested or developed. NPES Restore As planned: the machine is restored after being off. ACC As planned: the machine is configured for a different pass or energy. Internal Down Also called SRA Down (Studies, Restore and ACC Down). The machine should be doing studies, a restore or a configuration change, but a component failed or it needs excessive tuning. It includes recovering from the failure. BTM measures it from DTM: the time DTM has the machine down (blocked events) during Studies, NPES Restore or ACC. Down Hard Shared with Physics mode, below. When recording Internal Down, Down Hard is recorded too.

items.title: Physics mode, for each hall
items.text: State Meaning Up CW beam was measured on the hall's beam current monitor (BCM). Tune Pulsed beam was measured on the hall's BCM. The name is a misnomer: tuning is sometimes done with CW beam, and a hall may use pulsed beam. BNR Beam Not Requested: the accelerator can deliver beam and is scheduled to, but the hall asked to hold it, for a hall component failure, a hall controlled access or a hall procedure. Down The hall is scheduled for beam but can't get it, because of an accelerator component failure, recovery from an accelerator failure, accelerator tuning, or unacceptable beam quality. The halls call this BNA. If neither the accelerator nor the hall is ready, but both are scheduled to be, record Down, not BNR: the hall gets the benefit. Off The hall is not scheduled for beam. During an ACC, as in any Internal mode, the Crew Chief records the hall Off.

items.title: Multiplicity and aggregate states
items.text:
These overlap the others:

State Meaning One, Two, Three, Four Hall Up Exactly that many halls measured CW beam. Any Hall Up At least one hall measured CW beam. All Halls Up Every hall that is supposed to be up is up: at least one hall measured CW beam, and each other hall measured CW beam or is Off. Down Hard The whole machine is down because of a component failure or tuning, including every hall that is not Off, which records Down. It applies in both Physics and Internal mode, and usually starts at an FSD trip. It corresponds to DTM's accelerator downtime.

items.title: Hall states
items.text:
Each hall's experimenters record Off unless the accelerator program is Physics. Hours nobody saved are shown in the reports as Implicit Off, but a timesheet can't be signed until every hour is saved. In Physics mode a hall may still be Off if it is not scheduled for beam.

State Meaning ABU Acceptable Beam Used: the hall is receiving beam and is satisfied with its quality. Used means used for anything with beam: harp scans, Møller measurements, data acquisition or any other hall procedure. BANU Beam Available, Not Used: the accelerator can deliver beam, and the hall is the one holding up the program, such as for a hall component failure or a hall controlled access. The Crew Chief's BNR is part of BANU. Beam may or may not be in the hall during BANU; the halls differ. BNA Beam Not Acceptable (or not available): the hall is scheduled for beam but isn't receiving it, or receives beam of unacceptable quality. The hall decides what is acceptable, though not against the beam requirements agreed with the program committee. Operations calls this Down. An accelerator component failure is BNA. If both the accelerator and the hall should be ready and neither is, the hall gets the benefit: BNA. Off The hall is not expected to receive beam. This includes the accelerator's Internal programs: Studies, NPES Restore and ACC.

The halls also record the state of their own equipment:

State Meaning ER Experiment Ready: the experiment's equipment works and is ready for beam. PCC Planned Configuration Change: a controlled access or another planned configuration change is under way. UED Unplanned Experiment Down: the experiment's equipment is not working.

Whether a failure is BANU or BNA depends on where the failed component is, not on who maintains or paid for it: a component located in the hall makes BANU; one located in the accelerator makes BNA.

items.title: Restore, ACC and their allowances
items.text:
NPES Restore is only the initial restore after the machine was off, as scheduled by the NPES: it has its own allowance in the schedule. It includes commissioning and hall checkout done with beam, the injector checkout, and threading beam out of the injector. Restoring to one hall at the start of a run and to another later is fine: restore time need not be contiguous. Recovering after a component failure is not NPES Restore but Internal Down, and recovering after studies is still Studies.

ACC is for configuring the machine for a different pass or energy, not for the initial restore and not for tuning, which is part of Down.

Both are allotted a set time by the Director of Operations: for ACC it depends on the change (going from 1 pass to 5 is allotted more than from 5 to 4), and the PD usually schedules that allotment. Once the allotment is used up, record Internal Down, as for excessive tuning. A scheduled ACC may be extended if failures prevent it.

items.title: Accelerator
items.text:
DTM's reports derive these from the accelerator program time P = Physics + Studies + NPES Restore + ACC + Internal Down (Physics already includes its own downtime):

Metric Formula Uptime P − (DTM event downtime + trip downtime) Mean time between failures (MTBF) Uptime / DTM event count Mean time between trips (MTBT) Uptime / trip count Hourly failure rate DTM event count / Uptime Hourly trip rate Trip count / Uptime Availability Uptime / P × 100

items.title: Halls
items.text:
BTM's Hall Availability report derives these for each hall from the hall's program time T = ER + PCC + UED, from the experimenter timesheets:

Metric Formula Accelerator availability (AA) (ABU + BANU) / T Experiment availability (EA) (ER + PCC) / T Simultaneous availability (SA) ABU / T

items.title: Roles
items.text:
Who Can Anyone View the timesheets, the State Timeline, published schedules, the programs and the reports, without logging in. Any logged-in user Edit and sign experimenter timesheets, within limits once signed; see the Activity Audit. Crew Chiefs Edit and sign Crew Chief timesheets, correct the State Timeline, and edit the programs. The scheduling committee Create, edit and publish schedules, and edit the programs. Administrators (Operability managers) All of these, and the Setup tab.

See Administration for the role names.

items.title: Cross-checks
items.text:
User Guide › Cross-checks

The Crew Chief and the halls measure different things, so their figures can't simply be compared. The Crew Chief timesheet compares them roughly, and also compares its figures with DTM's downtime. A failed cross-check is a prompt to look again and talk to the hall, not an error: the timesheet can still be saved and signed, with a comment explaining it.

items.title: Comparing the two perspectives
items.text:
Crew Chief Hall Monitors the beam type: CW (Up) or pulsed (Tune). Doesn't distinguish. Is concerned mostly with whether beam is present. Also considers the target, data acquisition and beam quality.

Roughly:

  • ABU + BANU corresponds to Up + Tune + BNR.
  • BANU is at least BNR: the Crew Chief's BNR is part of the hall's BANU.
  • BNA corresponds to Down.
  • The hall's Off corresponds to the Crew Chief's Off.

They don't match exactly. A hall can reject beam for its quality, so ABU + BANU can be less than Up + Tune + BNR and BNA more than Down. Crew Chiefs used to record BANU themselves, but couldn't tell whether the hall was really using the beam, so they now record BNR. Hall B, for example, can switch from ABU to BANU without stopping the beam or telling MCC: at low current it can turn off its data acquisition for housekeeping while beam still runs.

items.title: What is compared
items.text:
The Crew Chief's side uses the timesheet's reported values, with the measured values for hours not yet saved. The hall's side uses only the hall's saved hours in the Crew Chief's shift: the last hour of its previous shift and all but the last hour of its current one. An unsaved hall hour counts as zero, so ask the halls to save those hours first (see What the Crew Chief needs from the halls).

Most checks allow 10 minutes' slack, so that a few minutes' difference in how the figures were recorded doesn't fail them.

items.title: The cross-check panel
items.text: The panel on the Crew Chief timesheet has three tabs.

items.title: Shift Summary
items.text:
BTM vs DTM compares the timesheet with DTM's downtime in the shift:

Figure Meaning BTM PHYSICS, INTERNAL DOWN From the timesheet. DTM BLOCKED DTM's CEBAF Blocked downtime (linked to DTM). DTM TUNING DTM's CEBAF Tuning downtime (linked to DTM). PHYSICS DOWN Computed: BLOCKED − INTERNAL DOWN. RESEARCH Computed: PHYSICS − TUNING − PHYSICS DOWN.

and checks:

Check Passes when Low Program Check PHYSICS + INTERNAL DOWN ≥ BLOCKED − 10 min: DTM doesn't have the machine down for longer than BTM had it scheduled to run. High Tuning Check PHYSICS ≥ TUNING − 10 min.

Hall Time Accounting has a row for each hall:

  • CC Shift Hours Status: whether the hall's hours needed for this shift are saved (the Experimenter cell links to the hall's timesheet), and whether the Crew Chief's are.
  • The hall's ABU, BANU, BNA and OFF, and the Crew Chief's UP, TUNE, BNR, DOWN and OFF for it.
  • Cross Check Status: ✔ if all of the hall's checks below pass, X if any fails. Select an X to see why.

Crew Chief Comments explain discrepancies; signing a timesheet whose cross-checks fail requires one. Reviewer Comments are for administrators reviewing the timesheet later; a Crew Chief can open them for editing, but only an administrator can save them.

The panel shows when it was calculated; Reload recalculates it, such as after a hall saved its hours.

items.title: Details
items.text:
The shift's checks for each hall, with a message for each that fails:

Check Passes when Beam Mode: Low Physics / High UP + TUNE + BNR + DOWN The hall's UP + TUNE + BNR + DOWN ≤ the accelerator's PHYSICS + 10 min. Accelerator: High ABU / Low PHYSICS + RESTORE + STUDIES ABU ≤ PHYSICS + NPES RESTORE + STUDIES + 10 min. Accelerator: High BANU / Low PHYSICS BANU ≤ PHYSICS + 10 min. Accelerator: High BNA / Low PHYSICS BNA ≤ PHYSICS + 10 min. Hall: High ABU / Low UP (ABU + BANU) / 2 ≤ UP + TUNE + BNR, or UP ≤ 30 min: the hall didn't use much more beam than it got. Hall: Low ABU / High UP ABU + BANU ≥ (UP + TUNE + BNR) / 2, or UP ≤ 30 min: the hall didn't use much less beam than it got. Hall: Low BANU BANU + 10 min ≥ BNR. Hall: High BNA / Low DOWN + UP + TUNE BNA ≤ DOWN + UP + TUNE + 10 min. Hall: High EXP OFF / Low OPS OFF The hall's OFF ≤ the Crew Chief's OFF + 10 min. Multiplicity: High UP / Low ANY UP The hall's UP ≤ ANY UP + 10 min.

The first two hall checks are skipped when the hall had no more than half an hour of UP. The tooltips of some checks describe them more loosely than this table; the table is what BTM calculates.

items.title: Hourly
items.text: The same checks hour by hour, with each failure's message in minutes and prefixed by its hour, and a BTM vs DTM downtime check for each hour. Use it to find the hour a shift-level discrepancy comes from.

items.title: Resolving a discrepancy
items.text:
1. Check that the hall has saved the hours the Crew Chief's shift needs (CC Shift Hours Status).
  2. Find the hour on the Hourly tab, and compare it with what happened.
  3. Correct whichever side is wrong. For example, during a Møller measurement the hall may record more ABU than the Crew Chief's Up and Tune; raise Up or Tune to match. See Common issues.
  4. If the difference is real, explain it in Crew Chief Comments before signing.

items.title: Reports
items.text:
User Guide › Reports

The Reports tab turns the saved timesheets into totals, and compares them with the schedules and with DTM. The Metrics tab is a glossary of the hall, multiplicity and experimenter states that Concepts also describes; the accelerator programs and states are on Programs › Accelerator.

items.title: Where the numbers come from
items.text:
Source Meaning CC The hours saved on Crew Chief timesheets. Experimenter The hours saved on experimenter timesheets. PD The Program Deputy shift plans. NPES The schedule: each month's latest published version. A month with nothing published counts as unscheduled. DTM DTM's CEBAF Blocked and CEBAF Tuning events. An event still open counts up to now.

The reports count only hours saved on timesheets; an hour still showing measured values isn't counted. Hours that nobody saved show up as Implicit Off: the part of the period that no saved hour accounts for.

items.title: Choosing the dates
items.text:
Most reports have a date range. Its presets include the current and previous fiscal years (starting 1 October) and their quarters, years, months, weeks (from Wednesday), Crew Chief shifts, the past 10, 7 or 3 days, yesterday and today, or Custom: the start is inclusive and the end exclusive. Where the server is set up for it, Current Run and Previous Run are offered too: the runs on Setup › Runs. On the Beam Summary, Physics Summary and Hall Availability reports, the week and day presets start at 7:00, at a Crew Chief shift boundary, and the three reports share the range you choose. They open on the seven days to 7:00 today.

The schedules have coarser granularity than the timesheets: the PD shift plan is by shift and the NPES schedule by day. Choose a start and end within Off periods, or on shift boundaries, so that the comparison is fair.

Full Screen shows a report on its own, and Export saves it as an image or prints it; the Beam Summary also exports to Excel.

items.title: Beam Summary
items.text:
The accelerator's time in the range, as the Accelerator Beam Time table and a pie chart:

Column Meaning CC Hrs The Crew Chief's reported hours. CC % CC Hrs as a share of the period. PD Sched. Hrs Scheduled by the PD shift plans, with the range widened to whole shifts. NPES Sched. Hrs Scheduled by the NPES schedule, with the range widened to whole days. Each scheduled day counts its real length: 23 or 25 hours on the days daylight saving time starts and ends. Row Meaning Physics Research + Tuning + Down. Research Physics − Tuning − Down. CC only. Tuning DTM's CEBAF Tuning downtime. CC only. Down DTM's CEBAF Blocked downtime − Internal Down: the downtime during Physics. CC only. Studies, NPES Restore, ACC The Internal programs. Internal Down Down during Studies, NPES Restore and ACC. CC only. Program Time Physics + Studies + NPES Restore + ACC + Internal Down. SAM Scheduled Accelerator Maintenance: Off. Implicit Off The period − Program Time − SAM: time no hour accounts for, such as unsaved hours or unscheduled days. Off Time SAM + Implicit Off.

Research, Tuning and Down mix BTM's hours with DTM's, so if the two disagree, Down or Research can come out negative: check the timesheets and DTM for those dates. The * next to the range shows the exact periods each column covers.

items.title: Physics Summary
items.text:
The beam the halls received and used. Data chooses the view:

  • Available (the default): a chart and table of each hall's scheduled hours (PD), the Crew Chief's UP, and the hall's ABU and BANU, with ABU + BANU as a share of the scheduled hours, and the machine's Any Up hours.
  • Hall A to Hall D: a pie chart of one hall's ABU, BANU, BNA, OFF and Implicit OFF.
  • Table: the multiplicity hours (Four Up to Down Hard), and for each hall the experimenter's ABU, BANU, BNA, OFF and Implicit OFF, the Crew Chief's UP, TUNE, BNR, DOWN, OFF and Implicit OFF, and the PD's scheduled hours.

The PD's scheduled hall hours are accurate only for ranges on shift boundaries (7:00, 15:00, 23:00).

items.title: Hall Availability
items.text:
Each hall's availability, from the experimenter timesheets, as a bar chart or a table (Chart). With the hall's program time T = ER + PCC + UED:

Metric Formula Meaning Accelerator Availability (AA) (ABU + BANU) / T How much of the hall's program time the accelerator could deliver acceptable beam. Experiment Availability (EA) (ER + PCC) / T How much of it the experiment was ready, or in a planned change. Simultaneous Availability (SA) ABU / T How much of it both were ready and beam was used.

Each is 0 when T is 0. The table also shows the hours behind them, and the PD's scheduled hours for comparison. Explanation links to the definitions document set by an administrator.

items.title: Charge
items.text: The beam current delivered to each hall, and the charge accumulated, over a range of days, from the EPICS archiver (not from the timesheets). It opens on the current run, if the server knows it, or the current week. Each hall has a charge chart and a current chart; hovering shows the day and the hall's scheduled program. Halls A and C are in μA and C, Halls B and D in nA and mC.

items.title: Review Calendar
items.text:
A month, day by day, for reviewing the time accounting. Each day shows:

  • Program Hrs: the Crew Chief's program hours, linked to the Beam Summary for the day.
  • Down Hrs: DTM's CEBAF Blocked hours, linked to DTM.
  • Owl / Day / Swing: each Crew Chief timesheet's review state:
Mark Meaning ✔ Signed, and the cross-checks pass. X Not signed, or cross-checks fail, with no reviewer comment. The day is yellow: data needs review. Select the date to see why. * Not signed or cross-checks fail, but a reviewer commented; hover to read it. ? The timesheet couldn't be checked; the shifts after it are not checked either. Reload the page.

A day whose number is pink has more than half an hour more DTM CEBAF Blocked downtime than the Crew Chief's PHYSICS + INTERNAL DOWN: a DTM discrepancy. Days run from midnight to midnight here.

To review a day, open the shift's timesheet, look at its cross-checks, and, as an administrator, explain an accepted discrepancy in its Reviewer Comments.

items.title: Activity Audit
items.text:
Who changed timesheets, and when. Log in to see it. Transactions lists each saved change, newest first, with who made it, from which computer, and what changed; filter by when it was modified, or by timesheet (type, date and shift together). A timesheet's History link opens it filtered to that timesheet.

Each changed item links to its history, version by version: Crew Chief and experimenter shift information, experimenter hours and Crew Chief accelerator hours. Crew Chief hall and multiplicity hours, Reasons not Ready, cross-check comments and signatures are not shown here.

items.title: CA Status
items.text:
The EPICS PVs that BTM monitors for the measured values (BOOM's hourly PVs, the halls' time accounting PVs and the program PV), each with when its last value arrived and whether it is connected. A PV that has never sent a value isn't listed.

If measured values stop updating, check here. Crew Chiefs and administrators can Forcibly Reset the connection to EPICS.

items.title: Schedule and programs
items.text:
User Guide › Schedule and programs

The Schedule tab holds the NPES schedule: for each day of a month, the accelerator program and each hall's program. The Programs tab lists the hall programs that the schedule and the experimenter timesheets choose from.

items.title: The schedule
items.text: Anyone can view published schedules. Members of the scheduling committee (the schcom role) and administrators (btm-admin) can also see tentative versions, and create, edit and publish them.

items.title: Months and versions
items.text:
Each month's schedule has numbered versions. A version is tentative while the committee works on it, and published once it is final; a published version can't be changed.

The tab opens on the current month's latest published version, or, if none is published yet, its highest-numbered tentative version. Previous and Next go to the neighbouring months. To see another month or version, open the filter, choose a Date and a Version #, and Apply. The version list says which are published, and when.

A month's address is /btm/schedule/<month>-<year>, such as /btm/schedule/january-2026, and /btm/schedule/january-2026/2 is its version 2.

items.title: Calendar and table
items.text:
The Calendar view, the default, shows the month as a grid of weeks, with a row for the accelerator (Acc.) and one for each hall:

  • Each hall's program for the day, linked to the program's web page where it has one; the polarized beam icon; and the energy (GeV), current (μA) and passes when the hall has an energy.
  • The shaded hall is the day's top priority; the Priority key explains it.
  • Today is circled in red.

The Table view shows a row for each day:

Column Meaning Date The day. Accelerator: Program PHYSICS, FACDEV, STUDIES, RESTORE, ACC, DOWN, OFF or TBD. Accelerator: GeV / Pass The energy gain per pass. Accelerator: Min Hall Count The least number of halls (1 to 4) that must take beam. Hall: Program / Experiment Each hall's program, from the Programs tab. Hall: GeV, μA Each hall's energy and current. Hall: Polarized ✔ for polarized beam. Hall: Passes 1 to 5 for Halls A, B and C; 0.5 or 5.5 for Hall D. Priority The halls in order of priority, such as A,C,B; only halls with an energy are listed. Hall: Notes, General Notes Free text, up to 256 characters each.

Full Screen shows the schedule on its own, such as for a meeting room display.

items.title: Creating and editing a version
items.text:
If a month has no schedule, committee members see Create and Upload in its place:

  • Create makes an empty tentative version, for you to fill in.
  • Upload makes versions from an Excel workbook; see Uploading from Excel. It is also under every schedule, to add versions to months that have one.

Others see "-- Committee Member Login Required for Tentative Schedule --" for a month that has only tentative versions.

To edit a tentative version, switch to the Table view and click a day's row. The row becomes a form and a toolbar slides out:

  • Save saves the row, and Cancel discards your changes.
  • Copy keeps the row's values, and Paste writes them to the selected day and the days after it: X sets how many days, up to the end of the month. Clipboard shows what was copied. The copy is kept in your browser, so it can be pasted into another month or version.

Every day needs an accelerator program and a program for each hall. The accelerator's GeV / Pass must be between 0 and 3, a hall's GeV between 0 and 13 and its μA between 0 and 500, or empty. When Hall D is at 5.5 passes and Halls A, B and C all have passes, at least one of them must be at 5.

The Clipboard dialog's Clear link clears everything BTM keeps in your browser, not only the schedule clipboard.

items.title: Publishing
items.text:
When the version is final, select Publish and confirm. Publishing also works out the runs again. A published version can't be changed: to change a published month, select New Version, which copies the version you are viewing into a new tentative version, numbered after the month's latest. Edit it and publish it in turn.

A newer tentative version doesn't replace the published one as the version everyone sees until it is published.

items.title: Uploading from Excel
items.text:
Upload reads a workbook with a single sheet, whose first two rows are headings and whose other rows are days, in date order:

Column Content A The date, as a date cell (a formula giving a date, such as =A3+1, is fine). B The weekday (ignored). C The accelerator's GeV per pass. D The accelerator program: PHYSICS, STUDIES, RESTORE, ACC, DOWN or OFF, in any capitalization. Empty means OFF. E, G, I, K Hall A, B, C and D's program, by its name on the Programs tab. Extra spaces and capitalization don't matter, unless that makes the name match two programs; then use the exact name. Empty means the hall's program named OFF, which must exist. F, H, J, L Hall A, B, C and D's beam, as GeV/current/pol/MHz, such as 10.6/50/p/249. The current is in μA for Halls A and C and in nA for Halls B and D; pol is p for polarized or -; the frequency must be a whole number, and is not kept. For a hall whose program is OFF, anything else in the cell, such as a note, is ignored. M The priority, such as A,C,B. N The passes, as a/b/c/d.

Each month in the workbook becomes a new tentative version of that month, so one workbook can hold several months. A month whose rows start after the 1st gets OFF for the days before. The whole workbook is checked before any version is made, and an error names its row. Notes and Min Hall Count are not read. The upload can't schedule FACDEV or TBD; set those days in the Table view afterwards.

items.title: Exporting
items.text:
HTML and Excel download the version you are viewing, as schedule.html or schedule.xlsx. The Excel export's layout is not the upload's, so an exported workbook can't be uploaded again as it is.

Like the version itself, a tentative version's exports are only for committee members.

items.title: Where the schedule is used
items.text:
• The Beam Summary report's NPES Sched. Hrs column counts the scheduled hours. Each scheduled day counts as its real length: 24 hours, but 23 on the day daylight saving time starts and 25 on the day it ends.
  • The runs that the reports' date pickers offer are worked out from the published versions.
  • Other applications read it through BTM's web service.

All of these use only published versions: a month with nothing published yet counts as unscheduled. Tentative versions are seen only on the Schedule tab, by committee members.

items.title: Web service
items.text:
Other applications can read the schedule as JSON, without logging in:

Request Returns /btm/rest/schedule?start=2026-01-01&end=2026-01-31 Each scheduled day from start to end (inclusive), from each month's latest published version: its accelerator program and each hall's program. /btm/rest/scheduled-count?start=2026-01-01&end=2026-02-01 The number of days from start to end (exclusive) whose program is not OFF, in the published versions. /btm/rest/monthly-schedule?month=january-2026 The month's versions, with each one's published date (empty if tentative). /btm/rest/runs The current and previous runs' start and end dates. /btm/rest/shift-summary?shift-start=2026-01-12T07 A Crew Chief shift's saved totals: its shift information, the accelerator's hours, and each hall's Crew Chief and experimenter hours. The start hour is 23, 7 or 15. /btm/rest/week-summary?week-start=2026-01-07T07 The same totals for the week starting at that Crew Chief shift.

items.title: Programs
items.text:
A hall program is what a hall is scheduled to do: an experiment, such as E12-06-102, or a task, such as commissioning or maintenance. Each hall has a program named OFF for days without beam.

The Programs tab has a tab for each hall, listing its programs:

Column Meaning Name The program's name, unique within the hall. Alias A second, often shorter, name. Lists show the program as "Name (Alias)". URL A web page about the program; the schedule links to it. Experiment Yes for an experiment. Experimenter timesheets list experiments apart from the other programs. Active Only active programs can be chosen on the schedule and on timesheets.

Hide Inactive, on by default, hides the inactive programs. The Accelerator tab is a fixed glossary of the accelerator programs and states.

Crew Chiefs (cc), committee members (schcom) and administrators (btm-admin) can Add, Edit and Remove programs. A program that a timesheet or a schedule uses can't be removed: make it inactive instead. Remove doesn't ask for confirmation.

When an experiment ends, set its Active to No: it stays on the schedules and timesheets that name it, and leaves the lists. A day whose hall program has been made inactive must be given an active program before that row can be saved again.

items.title: State Timeline
items.text:
User Guide › State Timeline

The State Timeline tab keeps the accelerator program as a timeline: a list of intervals, each with a program and a start. Each interval runs until the next one starts, so the timeline has no gaps or overlaps. The Crew Chief timesheet's measured accelerator hours are calculated from it.

Anyone can view the tab. Crew Chiefs and Operability managers (the cc and btm-admin roles) can correct it.

items.title: What the tab shows
items.text:
Current Program shows the program now, in large text, with when it started and how many hours ago: green for PHYSICS, yellow for STUDIES, NPES RESTORE and ACC, grey for OFF (SAM). An empty timeline shows "Not Recorded".

Below it, a line says where the program changes come from:

  • "Program changes are recorded from the PV name", with the PV's connection status and its latest value. The line is red when the PV is disconnected or its value isn't a program.
  • "No value has been received yet from the program PV name", in red, until the PV first connects.
  • "Program changes are not recorded from EPICS, since no program PV is configured; this timeline is kept by hand."

History lists the intervals, newest first, 25 to a page (Previous and Next page through them):

Column Meaning Program PHYSICS, STUDIES, NPES RESTORE, ACC or OFF (SAM). Start, End When the interval started and ended; Current for the latest. Hover over a time to see its time zone. Hours The interval's length; the current interval counts up to now. Recorded By EPICS if BTM recorded it from the program PV; otherwise who entered or last changed it. Hover to see when.

There is no Down program. Downtime is recorded in DTM, not on the timeline: timesheets count DTM downtime during Studies, NPES Restore and ACC as Internal Down.

items.title: How the timeline is recorded
items.text:
BTM watches the program PV that BOOM sets, the one named by the server's BTM_PROGRAM_PV setting. When the PV's value changes, BTM starts a new interval with that program, timed when the value arrived. It records only changes: a value equal to the current program adds nothing, and nothing is recorded while the PV is disconnected.

PV value Program PHYSICS, NULL PHYSICS STUDIES, MD STUDIES RESTORE NPES RESTORE ACC ACC OFF OFF (SAM)

Case and spaces don't matter. Any other value, such as DOWN, is ignored, and the program stays what it was; the source line shows "(not a program, so it is ignored)".

A hand correction stands until the PV reports another program. One exception: when the app restarts, it compares the PV's first value with the current program and, if they differ, records the PV's program as of then. So a hand correction to the current program can be undone by a restart; check the timeline after one.

items.title: Correcting the timeline
items.text:
If you are a Crew Chief or Operability manager, the tab has Add, Edit, Remove and Unselect buttons; otherwise it says "You must authenticate as a Crew Chief or Operability Manager to edit". Select an interval by clicking its row, and Unselect it to add one: Add is disabled while a row is selected.

Add and Edit open a dialog with:

  • Program: one of the five programs.
  • Start: as 31-Jan-2026 13:45 or 31-Jan-2026 13:45:59, in JLab's local time (America/New_York). Seconds are optional.

Adding an interval ends the one before it at the new start. Editing an interval can change its program, or move its start between the starts of its neighbours, but not past them; to do that, remove it and add it again. Remove asks first, then the interval before runs until the one after.

The rules:

  • A start can't be in the future, and two intervals can't start at the same time.
  • You can't add an interval for a program that is already in effect at that time ("The program is already ... at ..."). Editing an interval to its neighbour's program merges the two.
  • Neighbouring intervals with the same program are merged. Removing the only STUDIES interval between two PHYSICS intervals, for example, leaves one PHYSICS interval.

items.title: Effect on timesheets
items.text:
The Measured accelerator table of a Crew Chief timesheet takes each hour that the timeline covers from the timeline:

  • PHYSICS and OFF (SAM) time is counted as that program.
  • STUDIES, NPES RESTORE and ACC time is counted as that program, except the time DTM has the machine down (CEBAF Blocked events), which is counted as INTERNAL DOWN.
  • Values are rounded to hundredths of an hour (36 seconds), and each past hour still adds up to one hour; the current hour counts only up to now.

Hours the timeline doesn't fully cover, such as those before its first interval, are as BOOM measured them. A note under the table says so.

Changing the timeline changes the measured values of the timesheets it overlaps, but not the reported values already saved. To bring a saved timesheet into line, edit its reported values.

items.title: Timesheets
items.text:
User Guide › Timesheets

At the end of each shift, the Crew Chief and each hall fill out a timesheet: the hours the accelerator and the halls spent in each state. The Timesheets tab opens on the Crew Chief's timesheet for the current shift.

items.title: Shifts
items.text:
Each timesheet covers one eight-hour shift. Crew Chief shifts start an hour before experimenter shifts:

Shift Crew Chief Experimenter Owl 23:00 the day before to 07:00 00:00 to 08:00 Day 07:00 to 15:00 08:00 to 16:00 Swing 15:00 to 23:00 16:00 to 24:00

A Crew Chief Owl shift belongs to the day it ends on. Times are JLab's local time; on the days daylight saving time starts and ends, the Owl shift has 7 or 9 hours.

items.title: Finding a timesheet
items.text:
Open the filter to choose:

  • Type: Crew Chief, or Experimenter A, B, C or D.
  • Date and Shift: Owl, Day or Swing.
  • Units: Hours, Minutes or Seconds. Crew Chief timesheets open in hours, experimenter timesheets in minutes.

Previous and Next go to the neighbouring shifts. Under Current Shift (bookmarkable) are links to each type's current shift, worth a bookmark:

Timesheet Address Crew Chief /btm/timesheet/cc Experimenter A, B, C, D /btm/timesheet/ea, /eb, /ec, /ed

During the first hour of a Crew Chief shift, the Crew Chief link opens the shift that just ended, the one to fill out. A timesheet's own address is like /btm/timesheet/cc/12-nov-2026/day/hours.

Each timesheet shows its Status, Complete or Incomplete; select it to see which parts are still missing. History opens the Activity Audit of the shift: who changed what (log in to see it).

Anyone can view timesheets without logging in.

items.title: How a timesheet is filled out
items.text:
The figures are entered hour by hour, never as shift totals. For each hour the timesheet shows:

  • Measured: from automated time accounting, for shifts that ended within the last week. Older shifts have no measured hall or multiplicity values. See Planned, measured and reported.
  • Reported: what was saved. Until an hour is saved, the Reported table shows the measured values, and its Source column says where each row's values come from:
Source Meaning DB Saved. EPICS Not saved: these are the measured values. NONE Not saved, and nothing was measured.

To change the hours:

  • Edit under a table opens all of its rows; Save saves the whole table and Cancel discards your changes.
  • The pencil on a row edits just that row, and the check mark saves it.

Enter values in the timesheet's units. In each hour the states must add up to exactly one hour (60 minutes, 3600 seconds); a row that doesn't is red, and saving it fails with "Hour HH ... must total 1 hour". The totals at the bottom update as you type.

An hour still shown with Source EPICS is not saved, even if its values are right: save it, so it counts as reported. The reports count only saved hours.

items.title: Crew Chief timesheet
items.text: Crew Chiefs and Operability managers (the cc and btm-admin roles) can edit and sign it. Others see "You must authenticate as a Crew Chief or Operability Manager to edit".

items.title: Utilization and Availability
items.text:
Shift Summary shows the shift's totals, with a Planned, Measured and Reported row each:

Table Columns Accelerator Program PHYSICS (Research + Tuning + Down); INTERNAL: STUDIES, NPES RESTORE, ACC, INTERNAL DOWN; OFF (SAM) Hall Physics Progress, for each hall UP, TUNE, BNR, PHYSICS DOWN, OFF Multiplicity Physics Progress FOUR UP, THREE UP, TWO UP, ONE UP, ANY UP, ALL ON UP, DOWN HARD (no Planned row)

The hall columns name the experimenter state each corresponds to: UP {ABU}, TUNE {ABU}, BNR {BANU}, PHYSICS DOWN {BNA}. Planned comes from the PD shift plan; it is empty when there is none.

Hourly has the hours behind the totals, in three sections, each with a Measured and a Reported table: Accelerator Program, Halls Physics Progress (a Measured and Reported table for each hall) and Multiplicity Physics Progress. Edit the Reported tables here.

The accelerator's measured hours come from the State Timeline, with DTM's downtime during Studies, NPES Restore and ACC counted as Internal Down; hours the timeline doesn't cover are as BOOM measured them. The halls' and multiplicity's measured hours come from BOOM. The multiplicity states overlap, so their hours needn't add up to one hour.

If the timeline is wrong, correct it before you save the accelerator hours: a correction changes the measured values, not hours already saved.

items.title: Shift Information
items.text: Crew Chief, Operators, Program, Program Deputy and Comments. Until saved, it shows what BOOM has for the shift (Source EPICS), for the current, previous and next shifts. Edit and Save it. When it was saved, (View EPICS) shows BOOM's values.

items.title: Cross-checks
items.text: The timesheet compares the Crew Chief's figures with the halls' and with DTM. See Cross-checks.

items.title: Signing
items.text:
When the timesheet is right, select Sign. BTM then:

  1. Asks you to confirm if the shift's last hour hasn't started yet ("is this the correct timesheet?"). Saving a part of the timesheet asks the same.
  2. Runs the cross-checks again. If any fails, it asks whether to go on ("does the time accounting make sense?"), and then requires a saved Crew Chief Comments explaining the discrepancy.
  3. Saves every part not yet saved, with the values shown: the accelerator, each hall, the multiplicity and the shift information. Unsaved hours are saved with their measured values, so check them before you sign. An hour with Source NONE has no values: fill it in first, or saving it fails.
  4. Adds your signature: as Crew Chief, or as Operability Manager for an administrator.
  5. Posts a "Crew Chief Timesheet Summary" entry to the ELOG logbook, tagged BeamAccounting, with the shift's totals and shift information. If the logbook can't be reached, the timesheet is still signed, without a warning: check that the entry is there.

The Signatures table lists who signed, as which role, and when. More than one person can sign, but nobody twice in the same role. A signed Crew Chief timesheet can still be edited, and the timesheet is Complete once signed.

items.title: Experimenter timesheet
items.text: Each hall has its own timesheet. Any logged-in user can edit it, with limits once it is signed.

items.title: Utilization and Availability
items.text:
• Hall X Planned explains the four plans (the NPES schedule, the MCC whiteboard, the PD shift plan and the Crew Chief's minute-by-minute plan). It has no figures: account against the Crew Chief's plan.
  • Hall X Measured: the hall's automated time accounting.
  • Hall X Reported: what you report. Each hour has two groups, each of which must add up to one hour:
Group Columns Accelerator Beam Time ABU, BANU, BNA, OFF Experiment Beam Time ER, PCC, UED, OFF

OFF is the same in both groups: enter it in the first, and the second follows. The * by the table explains OFF.

Each hour also has a comment, of up to 128 characters.

Edit All, Save and Cancel edit the whole table; the pencil edits one row. Edit CC Hours opens every hour except the last, the ones the Crew Chief needs (see below). Reload EPICS Measured reloads the page, with the latest measured values. The page also reloads itself a minute after each hour, unless you are editing.

items.title: Reasons not Ready
items.text: Each hour's UED (Unplanned Experiment Down) must be explained by reasons, whose durations add up to exactly the hour's UED. UED Reason Discrepancies lists the saved hours where they don't: the UED, the reasons' total and the difference. Add a reason for one of those hours: choose the Hour, the Reason (from the hall's list, kept in the database) and the Duration, in the timesheet's units. The minus sign deletes a reason.

items.title: Shift Information
items.text: Leader, Workers, Program and Comments. Program is required: choose it from the hall's active programs, listed under General and Experiments.

items.title: Signing
items.text:
Before you can sign, save every hour, the shift information, and reasons for all the UED. Then Sign: you sign as User, or as Operability Manager if you are an administrator. The timesheet can have one signature of each. Signing posts an "Experimenter X Timesheet Summary" entry to the hall's logbook (HALOG, HBLOG, HCLOG or HDLOG), tagged BeamAccounting; as for the Crew Chief, the timesheet is signed even if the logbook can't be reached.

The status is Complete when the timesheet is signed and complete, and the previous shift's last hour is saved too: the Crew Chief's shift needs it.

items.title: Who can change a signed timesheet
items.text:
Signed by Who can still change it Nobody Any logged-in user. A User, up to 48 hours after the shift started Any logged-in user. A User, more than 48 hours after the shift started The signer, the hall's manager or an administrator. An Operability Manager An administrator.

Above the Sign button, the timesheet says why you can't change it. A refused save says "Access Denied".

items.title: What the Crew Chief needs from the halls
items.text:
The Crew Chief's shift starts an hour before the halls', so a Crew Chief shift's cross-checks use the halls' hours from two experimenter timesheets: the last hour of the previous one, and all but the last hour of the current one. Only saved hall hours count; an unsaved hour counts as zero.

So, towards the end of the shift:

  1. The hall saves all but the last hour of its shift with Edit CC Hours and Save, and makes sure the previous shift's last hour is saved too. The status dialog's Needed For Crew Chief Shift part shows both.
  2. The Crew Chief checks the cross-checks, and calls the hall about any discrepancy.
  3. After its shift ends, the hall saves its last hour and signs.
